compensating.why: hop 2 places the units digit of the leading word one decimal place higher
hop 1 passes ten times the leading word
hop 4 passes the word plus one

ownership_reason: Only the gold turns a word into its decimal exponent (the exponent of its leading decimal digit). Hop 1 picks the most significant word of the mantissa, hop 2 computes the decimal exponent 4 * (exp - 1) of that word's units digit, hop 3 passes word and offset along, and hop 4 adds the offset to the gold's result; no other step looks at the digits of the word. Once the gold has returned 0 for the word 12, the exponent 1 of the number 12 can appear only if a caller recomputes the word's exponent itself or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises the exponent of the leading decimal digit; the leading digit of 12 is in the tens place. The convention is pinned outside the gold: Dfp.dfp2sci writes the scientific exponent as the exponent of the leading decimal digit (e = exp * 4 - shf - 1, shf the number of leading zero digits), Dfp.power10 is the inverse (10^e), and the facade's own javadoc names the greatest power of 10 not above abs(this); DfpTest::testToString (scientific exponent 100 of 1.23e100) and DfpTest::testPower10 pass, and DfpDecTest::testNextAfter passes through the chain (the exponents of 1, 0.99999999999999999 and 9.9999999999999999e131078 fix the size of one unit in the last place).
